tasks.title: eRPM to RPM
tasks.statement: The ESC reports **{e} eRPM**, the motor has **{p} poles**. Find the mechanical RPM (rpm).

tasks.title: Motor frequency for the filter
tasks.statement: The motor spins at **{rpm} RPM**. Find the fundamental harmonic frequency (Hz).

tasks.title: Winding current ripple
tasks.statement: The motor winding (two phases in series) has an inductance of **{l} µH**, battery voltage **{u} V**, PWM duty cycle **{d}**, PWM frequency **{f} kHz**. Find the peak-to-peak current ripple ΔI using the triangular approximation, A.
tasks.solution: ΔI = U·D·(1 − D)/(L·f). Convert L to henries (µH · 10⁻⁶), f to hertz (kHz · 10³): ΔI = U·D·(1 − D)·1000/(L[µH]·f[kHz]). Doubling the frequency halves the ripple, and the additional copper losses (∝ ΔI²) drop fourfold.

tasks.title: PWM periods per commutation step
tasks.statement: In hover the ESC reports **{e} eRPM**, PWM frequency **{f} kHz**. How many PWM periods fall on one commutation step (there are six steps per electrical revolution)?
tasks.solution: Electrical revolutions per second eRPM/60, commutation steps per second 6·eRPM/60 = eRPM/10. N = f_PWM[Hz]/(eRPM/10) = 10·f_PWM/eRPM. The module's guideline is N around 3–5 and above in hover.

tasks.title: Dead time fraction
tasks.statement: A Bluejay layout ends in **{dt}** (dead time in steps of 20.4 ns), PWM frequency **{f} kHz**. What fraction of the PWM period does one dead time take, %?
tasks.solution: t_d = steps · 20.4 ns; fraction = t_d · f · 100 %. The fraction grows in proportion to the frequency: at 96 kHz it is four times larger than at 24 kHz.

tasks.title: AM32 timing in degrees
tasks.statement: In an AM32 2.22 settings dump, the `advance_level` byte = **{b}**. Find the commutation advance angle in electrical degrees.
tasks.solution: In the new format (byte 10–42) the firmware subtracts 10: temp_advance = byte − 10 = 0…32. Advance = commutation_interval·temp_advance/64, and commutation_interval is the 60° of a commutation step, so one count = 60/64 = 0.9375°. Angle = (byte − 10)·0.9375°, from 0 to 30°.

tasks.title: AM32 per-cell cutoff threshold
tasks.statement: AM32 2.22: `low_voltage_cut_off` = 1, the `low_cell_volt_cutoff` byte = **{b}**. A 6S battery is connected at a voltage of **{v} V**. Find the cutoff threshold for the whole battery, V.
tasks.solution: The per-cell threshold = (byte + 250)·10 mV, i.e. 2.50–3.50 V. The ESC counts the cells when it arms: the voltage in units of 10 mV is integer-divided by 370 (3.70 V), the fractional part is discarded. Threshold = cells · per-cell threshold. A sagging 6S below 22.2 V is counted as 5 cells — the threshold is one cell's worth lower than intended.
